levels.name: Maya, 24, Barista
levels.story: Level 1: 1,200 dollars a month, and my family just removed me from the group chat. I am Maya, 24, a part-time barista living in a cramped studio apartment. My fingers are stained from peeling onions all day at the local deli, and my forehead badge glows a pathetic 1,200. Today, the family Thanksgiving group chat blew up with holiday pressure, flight cost debates, and luxury gift lists. I cannot even afford a bus ticket home. Then my aunt texted me directly: Don't bother showing up empty-handed. That sting hit deeper than any customer insult. Suddenly, my phone buzzed with an emergency rent subsidy deposit. My balance jumped instantly. Then my landlord called to demand the rest. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Leo, 27, Delivery Driver
levels.story: Level 2: 2,800 dollars a month, and my brother just publicly roasted my economy seat purchase. I am Leo, 27, a delivery driver constantly dodging traffic on my scooter. My skin is a tough, bumpy orange rind, smelling faintly of diesel and cold rain. In the family group chat, the holiday pressure is reaching boiling point. Everyone is comparing gifts and travel itineraries. I saved for months to buy a basic airline ticket to visit our parents. Then my brother messaged the whole chat: Enjoy sitting in the back with the cargo. His arrogance makes my blood boil. Suddenly, a hefty holiday bonus hit my account from night shifts. My forehead badge flickered and climbed. Then my dispatcher assigned me a triple holiday shift. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Chloe, 31, Accountant
levels.story: Level 3: 4,500 dollars a month, and someone just maxed out the family holiday dinner budget using my card. I am Chloe, 31, a meticulous accountant who crunches numbers until my head hurts. My head is a smooth, tart green apple, crisp and hyper-vigilant. The family group chat is absolute chaos; everyone is arguing over who brings the expensive organic turkey. I am trying to keep our holiday budget afloat without going into debt. Then my mother sent a voice note to the chat: Stop pinching pennies, this is for family. The disrespect after all my planning is unreal. Suddenly, an unexpected tax refund notification popped up on my screen. My forehead badge jumped instantly. Then my phone rang with an overdraft warning. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Sam, 35, High School Teacher
levels.story: Level 4: 6,200 dollars a month, and I just found out I was uninvited from the main family holiday bash. I am Sam, 35, a passionate history teacher with a head shaped like a firm brown coconut, tough on the outside, soft inside. My classroom is loud, but my apartment is quiet, filled with stacks of ungraded essays. In the family chat, the elite relatives are planning an exclusive luxury resort Thanksgiving, completely ignoring us middle-tier earners. I tried to offer a modest contribution, and my cousin replied instantly: Don't worry, we invited people who actually fit the vibe. The sheer exclusion burns. Suddenly, an unexpected school board stipend hit my account. My forehead badge flashed upward. Then the principal called me about a schedule change. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Elena, 39, Architect
levels.story: Level 5: 9,800 dollars a month, and someone just sabotaged my holiday toast video in the group chat. I am Elena, 39, an architect who designs sleek glass buildings. My head is a vibrant, scaly red dragon fruit, exotic and sharp-edged. The family holiday pressure is unbearable; everyone expects me to fund the entire venue rental because of my badge. In the chat, relatives are voting on my proposed venue layout. Then my uncle posted a doctored voice clip mocking my architectural presentation with the caption: Looks more like a prison than a dining room. The betrayal cuts deep. Suddenly, a major client approved my blueprint bonus. My forehead badge leaped forward. Then my contractor called with an emergency site delay. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Marcus, 42, Surgeon
levels.story: Level 6: 18,500 dollars a month, and my uncle just deleted the entire holiday contribution spreadsheet I spent hours making. I am Marcus, 42, a senior surgeon with a head shaped like a smooth, golden-yellow pineapple, spiky-crowned and imposing. In the family group chat, tensions are at an all-time high over who pays for the annual luxury family retreat. Everyone treats me like an ATM rather than a brother or son. I tried to organize a fair cost-split, and my aunt fired back in the chat: Stop acting like the CEO of our family. The disrespect stings after working eighty-hour weeks. Suddenly, my hospital direct deposit alert chimed with a massive hazard bonus. My forehead badge flashed upward. Then the chief of surgery paged me for an emergency consult. You'll see that in Level 7.
